published_results.claim: A Go-based command-line tool for benchmarking Ollama models with configurable parameters, warmup phases, TTFT tracking, VRAM monitoring, and benchstat/CSV output.
published_results.metric: Per-model prefill and generate rate (ns/token, tokens/s), time to first token, load time, total duration, model size and VRAM; a -decision mode reports accuracy, latency percentiles and requests/questions per second against an external JSONL corpus. Prompts can be sized from a bundled HumanEval set. The README's sample benchstat/CSV lines (e.g. 12800.00 and 51200.00 token/sec for gemma3) illustrate the output format.

published_results.claim: Smoke-run each benchmark once to catch panics and bit rot; this does ... not assert timings.
published_results.metric: 29 Go func Benchmark* outside vendored code (mlxrunner tokenizer encode/decode/load, mlx activation and top-k, dflash, flint precision, GGUF parsing, download/transfer, routes)

published_results.claim: `q8_0` - 8-bit quantization, uses approximately 1/2 the memory of `f16` ... `q4_0` - 4-bit quantization, uses approximately 1/4 the memory of `f16`
published_results.metric: K/V cache memory with OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE quantization (requires Flash Attention); nominal ratio stated without a measurement
published_results.value: q8_0: approximately 1/2 of f16; q4_0: approximately 1/4 of f16

published_results.claim: **Performance Gains**: Examples show significant speed improvements (e.g., 85.54 tokens/s vs 52.02 tokens/s) and full GPU layer utilization.
published_results.metric: Generation speed under Ollama's new model scheduling (September 23, 2025), as summarized inside an example model response to a web-search tool call; no model, hardware or source URL given in the repo

summary: Ollama publishes no measured results about its own performance in its README or docs. It ships a benchmarking CLI (cmd/bench: prefill/generate tokens/s, TTFT, load time, VRAM, plus an accuracy-scoring mode for decision models) and 29 Go micro-benchmarks that CI runs once without checking timings, but commits no output from either. The only figures about Ollama itself are the FAQ's nominal K/V-cache sizes (q8_0 approximately 1/2 and q4_0 approximately 1/4 of f16 memory) and an example web-search response in the docs quoting 85.54 tokens/s vs 52.02 tokens/s from Ollama's model-scheduling announcement.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
